limitations: Historical re-issue, not prospective validation: every interval is re-issued at a past origin from one frozen snapshot (a single final data vintage) and scored against recorded actuals.

The evaluation period is M2's confirmation period. Its point errors were examined in M2 (and the model was confirmed there), so it is not an untouched test; only the interval and probability results are new.

Forecast paths from neighbouring origins overlap and errors follow month-long regimes: thousands of scored forecasts are worth only tens of independent observations (see the HAC effective sample sizes). Coverage intervals and p-values are indicative.

Residual-based intervals assume that the errors of the calibration window describe the errors to come. Level shifts, growth and unusual periods (year-end) break this; split-conformal guarantees require exchangeability, which does not hold here.
Historical thresholds are percentiles of incoming demand, and hypothetical thresholds are user-supplied numbers. Neither is a measured service capacity of any NYC agency.

models.description: Modernised regression atlas-m2-regression-v1: 18 non-collinear M1 features plus intercept, OLS on standardised columns (full rank required), recursive, clipped at 0.
Median of the 5 most recent observed values on the target's weekday (on or before the origin).

protocol.eligibility_rule: residual.target_date <= calibration_origin - data_latency_days, with calibration_origin = issue origin (rolling) or the period's first origin (fixed)

periods.description: Interval-method selection. Starts six months after the first residual origin so that every horizon has at least 100 eligible calibration origins at the first issue; scores only M2 development-period targets (through 2025-06-30).
periods.name: m3_selection

periods.description: Historical evaluation of the sealed choice on the M2 confirmation origins (targets 2025-07-01..2026-06-30). Already exposed in M2: not an untouched prospective test.
periods.name: m3_evaluation

selection.reason: lowest mean WIS on the m3_selection period (457.914)
selection.rule: Among the candidate method/scheme pairs, those with an unavailable-forecast rate above max_unavailable_rate on the selection period are ineligible; the others are ranked by mean WIS over the selection horizons on the forecasts every eligible candidate issued, for the primary point model; ties go to the earlier candidate. The evaluation period never selects.

thresholds.description: 75th percentile (linear interpolation) of the observed daily counts in the 180 days ending at each forecast's data cutoff: the legacy 'planning capacity' rule recomputed at every origin. A high-demand reference derived from incoming requests, not a measured service capacity.
thresholds.label: trailing180_p75
thresholds.notice: Historical demand percentile: a high-demand reference computed from past incoming requests, not a measured service capacity.

thresholds.assumptions: Illustrative round number set above the legacy demand percentile of 11,609 requests per day. It is not derived from staffing, budgets, closures, backlog or service-level targets (none exist in the repository) and does not represent the capacity of any NYC agency; it only demonstrates how a user-supplied capacity threshold is handled.
thresholds.label: hypothetical_capacity_12000
thresholds.notice: HYPOTHETICAL threshold: a user-supplied number, not a verified NYC agency service capacity.

thresholds.assumptions: Second illustrative round number, 1,000 requests per day above the first, chosen without reference to any operational data; it does not represent the capacity of any NYC agency and exists to show that probabilities fall as the threshold rises.
thresholds.label: hypothetical_capacity_13000
thresholds.notice: HYPOTHETICAL threshold: a user-supplied number, not a verified NYC agency service capacity.
